segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for making time, Dana. I had us down to review the 42-seat rollout and the services line before I send the order form through deal desk.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Yep, that’s right. We’re still at 42 seats for phase one. The only change is we want the admin training split into two sessions instead of one, if that doesn’t move the price much.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: It doesn’t. The services package is still $6,800 total, we’d just schedule two 90-minute sessions the week of March 11. License is $38 per seat per month, annual term, so $19,152 for the subscription.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay, and the start date on that is March 1, correct? Our finance team asked because they don’t want an invoice dated in February.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Correct, March 1 start, March 1 invoice date. Net 30 terms, so payment due March 31. I’ll make sure that’s reflected in the billing tool and on the order form.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Great. For go-live, we’re targeting April 8. Is that still reasonable with the March 11 training?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, so if we get signature by February 23, we can do kickoff March 4, training March 12 and 14, and leave about three weeks for configuration and user testing. April 8 is reasonable.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Sounds good. One thing on the contract: legal asked if the auto-renewal can be 30 days notice instead of 60.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: That’s within our standard fallback. I’ll note 30 days’ notice for non-renewal in the special terms and have deal desk approve it. No pricing impact.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Perfect. Send it to me and I’ll route it for signature. If I have it today, I can probably get it back by next Wednesday.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: I’ll send it this afternoon, along with the implementation timeline and the seat breakdown by department. You’ll see 18 operations, 14 customer support, and 10 managers on the quote.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Yep, that matches our list. Thanks, Mark.
